lines.text: Riya demos her PDF bot in an interview. The interviewer asks just one question: how do you know it works?
Three hand-picked questions are not an answer. A small test set and a few numbers are.
Step one: write a golden set. Twenty to thirty questions, each with a reference answer and the page it lives on.
Include a few the document cannot answer. The right behaviour there is: I don't know.
Step two: measure retrieval. For each question, did the right page appear in the top four chunks? That is hit rate at four.
Step three: measure the answer. A second model acts as judge: is every claim supported by the retrieved context? That is faithfulness.
Now the numbers tell you where to work. Low hit rate: fix retrieval. High hit rate but low faithfulness: fix the prompt.
Change one thing at a time, re-run, and write the result in your README.
So when someone asks how you know it works, don't say it seems fine. Show the numbers.
Next module: agents and tool calling.
